findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with the insert, so the limit can be exceeded
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a separate CountDevices query followed by an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. Two (or more) concurrent requests — on the same or different Grafana instances sharing a database — can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. Since anonymous auth requests are inherently concurrent, the configured device_limit is only approximate. Enforcement needs to be atomic (e.g., conditional insert in a single statement or a transaction with appropriate isolation) or the limitation should be documented.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from async goroutine into the synchronous anonymous auth path
findings.body: Previously TagDevice ran in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout; this PR calls it synchronously in Authenticate. Every anonymous request that misses the 29-minute local cache now performs a COUNT query plus a write to the anon_device table inline before the request is authenticated. On a busy instance with many distinct devices, this adds database latency (and DB load from the extra COUNT on every uncached request) to every anonymous page load, and a slow/unavailable database now delays or breaks anonymous authentication, which was previously immune to tagging failures.

findings.title: ErrDeviceLimitReached aborts authentication with a raw internal error
findings.body: When the device limit is reached, Authenticate returns nil plus the raw sentinel error ErrDeviceLimitReached ("device limit reached"). This propagates through authn as a generic authentication failure, so an anonymous user hitting the limit gets an unexplained 500/internal error instead of a meaningful response. Also note the device is already cached in tagDeviceUI's localCache before the DB write fails, so the failure (and error) only surfaces on the first request per device per ~29 minutes — subsequent requests silently authenticate while the device is never recorded. If rejecting users past the limit is intended, the error should be surfaced as a deliberate user-facing message; if not, the error shouldn't fail authentication.

findings.title: Existing devices with stale updated_at get ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being refreshed
findings.body: Once the limit is reached, updateDevice only updates rows whose updated_at falls within [now-30d, now+1m]. A device that exists in anon_device but hasn't been seen for over 30 days (rows are only purged after 61 days by the cleanup job) matches no rows, RowsAffected == 0, and ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned — even though that device's own stale slot could legitimately be reused. The upsert path that would have refreshed it is skipped entirely once count >= deviceLimit.

findings.title: New device_limit option not documented in sample config
findings.body: The new [auth.anonymous] device_limit setting is read but no corresponding entry/documentation appears to be added to conf/sample.ini or conf/defaults.ini alongside the other auth.anonymous options, so admins have no discoverable way to learn the option exists, its units, or that 0 means unlimited.
